_what: Synthetic Ruby bare-read gate for #3880 (RUBY-04), following bench/ruby-gem-resolution: exact accuracy cells and fingerprints, with ratios as the only timing gates. Real capture emitter, real parse worker (dist/), real Ruby ScopeResolver and manifest loader; analyze, persistence and full-pipeline memory are outside this benchmark.
_triage: Shape and fingerprint failures are deterministic: inspect the corpus and the resolved edges, never rebaseline just to make CI green. The runner also fails, before any baseline comparison, when a method misses an expected CALLS edge or gains one the source never makes. For a timing failure, rerun on an idle machine and verify the report shows its profile (ci: 5 interleaved samples after 1 warmup; full: 15 after 2) before investigating a regression. Millisecond observations are context, not gates.
_shape_note: Exact counts are the workload FLOOR. blocks: small 128 methods x depth 4, methods 512 x 4 (4x), depth 128 x 64 (16x). heredocs: small 64 methods x 2 heredocs per opener line x 2 reads per body, methods 256 x 2 x 2, per_line 64 x 8 x 2, size 64 x 2 x 8 (4x each). Every line has a fixed-width indent, so input_bytes (pinned per shape, beside capture_groups and relationships) grows linearly: blocks depth 35730 -> 365202 bytes (10.2x for 16x depth; the earlier two-spaces-per-level indent grew the input 47x over 4 -> 64). One class per file. Expected edges are computed from the source: every bare `target` that reads the parameter (in a block at any depth, or in a heredoc body) gets no edge; `helper` and `other(...)` stay calls; `other(<<~EOS, target = 1)` keeps the body's `target` as a call (the opener rule). main turns the parameter reads into wrong `Host<i>#target` edges (16 wrong at 16 x 4 blocks, 8 at 8 heredoc methods), so this gate fails without #3880.
_fingerprint_note: Hashes pin every relationship (endpoints, type, confidence, reason) and every decline (reason, file, name, position).
_scaling_note: Scaling ratios are (t_shape / t_small) / growth, where growth is 4, or 16 for blocks depth: about 1 is linear, about the growth factor is quadratic. Budget 1.5 applies to every capture and resolution ratio, including blocks_resolve_depth_scaling_ratio. Metric and budget keys must match exactly.
_depth_note: Capture and resolution are gated over the full depth range 4 -> 64. Capture indexes bound reads once per file and takes Ruby call arguments only from their own argument field. Read-only receiver and reference passes now path-compress empty lexical scopes, so the former depth-resolution gate exemption no longer applies. The bound-read shape does not cover preexisting ancestor walks for Ruby free calls with implicit receivers; those remain tracked in #3915.
_one_file_note: The crowded one-file shape (--shape crowded) is available for separate investigation and is not gated. Historical measurements below predate the shared lookup cache in this PR and do not describe its current resolution scaling.
_profiles_note: Two profiles share the shapes and every accuracy gate. CI (the default, and what --check runs in the benchmarks job): one process, one parse worker, every workload timed, min of 5 after 1 warmup, interleaved. --full: one child times every workload, min of 15 after 2 warmups, and each shape runs in a fresh child for its peak RSS. Wall times are in _measured_ci.
_negative_controls_note: Each is a temporary edit, measured in the CI profile with unchanged fingerprints. Restoring the per-read method climb (main's rubyBareNameIsLocalRead) fails blocks_capture_depth_scaling_ratio 3.872 > 1.5. Restoring the callable-flow subtree search (dropping Ruby's extractCallArguments) fails it at 1.792 > 1.5. On main's own bench (depth 4 -> 16, two-spaces-per-level indent) the per-read climb is the shipped code and passed at 1.222. Restoring the per-body heredoc opener search (O(H^2) per opener line) passes every timing ratio, even with 32 heredocs per line (heredocs_capture_per_line 0.565): per-method work hides it at CI sizes, so the operation-count unit test (test/unit/scope-resolution/ruby/ruby-bare-read-cost.test.ts: 12126 -> 72702 tree steps for 32 -> 128 heredocs before, 10046 -> 39806 after) is its guard. These are deliberate regressions, not baseline observations.
